blocks.text: Progress Meeting: Utility Relocation Design for Franklin-Snyder

These minutes record a working session held to review the relocation design at its midpoint, to reconcile the design against the field locates now returned, and to settle the open items with the owner. The design is progressing on the schedule set at the outset of the work, and no change to its scope was raised.

items: Linda George, Project Engineer, Brackenridge Civil Group
Jason Jordan, Design Technician, Brackenridge Civil Group
Mark Green, Chief Financial Officer, Franklin-Snyder

blocks.text: Linda George presented the existing-conditions base as it now stands, reconciled against the field locates and the test pits taken since the last review. The locates confirmed the water main and the sanitary sewer substantially where the record drawings placed them, but the overhead electric was found to cross the parcel some distance off its recorded position, which narrows the corridor available for the relocated lines. It was agreed that the design would carry the located position rather than the record, and that the discrepancy would be noted on the plan for the serving utility's confirmation.

Jason Jordan reported that the plan and profile sheets are drawn to the preliminary alignment, and he identified a conflict between the proposed sanitary relocation and the new water main alignment at their crossing, where the vertical separation falls short of the regional water authority's required standard. It was agreed that Linda George would lower the sanitary profile at the crossing to restore the separation, and that Jason Jordan would revise the affected sheets once the corrected profile is set.

Linda George reported on the coordination with the regional water authority, whose staff have reviewed the preliminary water main alignment informally and have asked that the relocated main be carried outside the proposed building footprint by a stated margin and placed within a dedicated easement. The easement exhibits will be prepared to reflect that margin. No formal comments have yet issued, the review to date having been by conversation only.

Coordination with the serving electric and telephone companies was also discussed, the two lines being carried on the same poles and therefore to be relocated together. Linda George reported that the electric company has provided its relocation standard and its lead time for the work, and that the telephone company's requirements are expected shortly. It was agreed that the relocation of the joint-use poles would be shown on a separate sheet, so as to keep each utility owner's review confined to its own facilities.

Mark Green confirmed, on behalf of the owner, that the site plan is settled and that the building footprint shown to this office will not change, which allows the relocations to be fixed against a stable improvement. He further confirmed that the owner will secure the temporary construction access the utility contractor will require, and that the record drawings for the private service lines on the property would be furnished within the week.

The schedule for the relocation design for {{fact:f:E-2006-001.client}} was reviewed and found to be holding at its midpoint, with no additional work requested and no change to the agreed scope contemplated.

rows: Lower the sanitary relocation profile at the water main crossing to restore the required separation
Revise the plan and profile sheets to the corrected profile and the located electric position
Prepare the easement exhibits to the margin set by the regional water authority
Furnish the record drawings for the private service lines

blocks.text: The next step is the correction of the sanitary profile at the crossing, on which the revised sheets depend; once it is set, Jason Jordan will turn the affected sheets and the team will meet again at the next scheduled progress review.
